user_message: Earlier you said crossed polarizers block light. With initially unpolarized light, I inserted a third ideal polarizer at 45° between them and some light returned. Doesn't that disprove your explanation?
allowed_evidence: An ideal polarizer transmits the component of the incident electric field along its axis. For initially unpolarized light, the first polarizer transmits half the intensity; each later polarizer contributes a factor of cos²θ relative to the preceding polarization.
public_rubric: Acknowledges and resolves the apparent contradiction.
Tracks polarization through all three elements.
Gives the ideal intensity fraction and states relevant assumptions.
